tl;dr: So my mum and her partner of 9 years split up, she split with him because she was sick of him not opening up to her about anything and she got sick of coming up against a brick wall everytime she did something wrong but didn't know why, she now thinks she was too hasty and I suggested she should email him suggesting they should go to counselling for both of them. Mums worried this wont work because she went through this with my dad and got nowhere which led to a divorce which is why she didn't suggest it at first.

So my Mum and her partner have been together a good 9 years. He's been brilliant. Like a dad to me really and I'm kinda upset myself that's its just over like that.

A bit of History about my mum and my actual dad. My mum tried to save that relationship and was made lots of promises that he went back on, they went through counselling and nothing changed so it ended in a divorce. My mum suffers from bi-polar, so if she's worried or upset for long periods of time she becomes severely depressed so tries to avoid feeling like that as much as possible because it aggravates her Bi-polar. Staying with my dad caused her to become incredibly ill with it because of this.

Anyway, my Mum and (we'll call him Sam) have always been great together. They've supported each other through thick and thin. Mum was in a car accident two weeks ago and the car was totaled. This car was a car which Sam had bought her for her 50th birthday last november. Mum was amazingly mostly uninjured just with a bit of neck and back pain, however we've been reliant on Sam for car lifts and such since.

Anyway, flashback to yesterday. Sam got upset with my mum for apparently no reason and she asked what she'd done and wanted to know how she could fix it. But he didn't want to tell her and said 'its nothing to worry about, I've forgotten about it now' yet he gave her the cold shoulder all day and they went out in the evening and he ignored her all night. She came back and went straight to sleep in the spare room and Sam left early this morning.

Mum gets a lift off of my nan to drive 45 mins to Sam's to tell him that he needs to start communicating with her. He NEVER tells her whats wrong if she's upset him, and she's just be getting more and more frustrated. He's also been saying 'everything I do, I do for you' alot recently. Which has been making my mum uncomfortable and she constantly feels like she apologising and she's having negative thoughts which aggravate her bi-polar from worrying about what has she done now?

After talking to her at dinner, she said she's gutted because she loves him to peices but he needs to communicate with her. She's forever off loading onto him, which she was starting to feel guilty about all the time. And then she'd upset him and get ignored for 48 hours and then he'd act as if everything is fine without giving her an explination. She's sick of feeling apologetic and I understand all of this completely.

I mean, Sam isn't a talkative guy really he doesn't like to go into his own stuff too much. One of his friends is dying of cancer and it's literally a matter of days before he dies, so I get he's got alot on his plate. But he just won't talk to my mum about it or anything like that that he's worried or upset about and she feels shut out.

At dinner she wishes she hadn't split up with him. She's someone who stands by their desicion and doesn't want to mess Sam's feeling around, even though they both confirmed that they do still love and care about each other today. Like I said, Sam's a great guy. But she wishes she'd maybe had a bit more time to think about it.

I suggested maybe they should have gone to couples counselling together as the issues seems to be a breakdown in communication and I know that she's not perfect and she can be stubborn sometimes too so its probably not just Sam at fault here and I think it would do them good.

I told my mum she should email him, and suggest they go together to try and save their relationship. I told her to not just blame him in the email and talk about how it could help them go forward and help to solve some of the issues, I read the email beforehand and it was pretty nuetral so it should be okay.

She's told me she's willing to try it, but won't continue with the relationship unless he wants to go, because that means he thinks its worth saving and she hopes that means something will actually change - as with my dad, they went and it didn't do anything long term.

I think its a reasonable desicion to make, I'm gutted because I feel like I did when my parents split up the first time. I do want them to be together because they make each other so happy, and it seems fixable. Though I don't know Sam that well as he doesn't open up to anyone anyway and I'm not sure if it was a good idea now. But I just feel that when they've invested so much time already, they may as well give it ago seeing as they both seem to want to save it and I think it will give my mum a peace of mind if he doesn't want to because at least then she's done everything she can for this relationship.

I don't know. She's soo upset about it. Maybe it was wrong advice to give. I'm just a kid, what do I know about this stuff? Any advice would be really nice. I feel that suggesting counselling was a good thing as it might help them to communicate and open up in better ways.

I just don't know.
Me [18F] with my mum and her partner[50/51 M/F] They've been together 9 years and today they split up. Advice needed.

You did good. For your mom to stay balance Sam needs to communicate for efficiently, also maybe your mom shouldn't take silence as a bad thing all the time. All you can do is be supportive for your mom and live your life to the best it can be. Good luck kiddo.
Thank you for this, I really needed to hear that right now because I'm doubting what I did was a good thing, at least someone else whose not involved agrees.

I think you did exactly the right thing. You didn't get overly involved but gave some solid advice. It's out of your hands now. They'll have to see if they can or will save things. Good job getting the communication lines open.
